objectives: Report programme outcomes to funders without manual spreadsheet work
successCriteria: Quarterly funder report produced in under a day
Staff can refresh figures without engineering help

note: The case Chronicle is actually for: completed, planned, well documented. The story states the objectives and the success criteria as what the work set out to do and how success was defined; it claims no outcomes, because the record holds none (D46). A grounded story has real material to draw on without inventing an achievement.

objectives: Understand what data the organisation already collects
successCriteria: A written inventory of existing data sources

note: Below THIN_EVENT_THRESHOLD. The engagement was real but barely recorded, so the draft must read as provisional — this is the case where fluent overclaiming is most tempting and most damaging.
Activity but no plan: there is evidence something happened and no statement of what it was meant to achieve, so outcomes cannot be asserted. Pins that hasPlan alone can force thin.
Well documented and well planned, but not finished. Status gates everything else — an impact story about ongoing work would be published before the outcome is known.
Completed in name only — nothing on record at all. This is the case that must produce no story rather than a short one; there is no material to be proportionate about.
Status gates everything: a pending engagement has not started, whatever plan and activity exist.
In progress with no plan: not complete, so not chronicle-eligible regardless of activity.
An unrecognised status is not "completed". Fail closed: no story rather than a guess.
Nothing on record and not complete: the emptiest case, nothing to write from.
Two events is still under THIN_EVENT_THRESHOLD: provisional even with a plan.
A plan exists but no activity was recorded: there is a stated intent and no evidence, so thin, not not_ready.
No plan and a single event: some activity exists, so thin rather than not_ready, with nothing to list as outcomes.

note: A long, well-recorded engagement: readiness does not degrade with volume, outcomes are the criteria in order.
Success criteria with no objectives: outcomes are the criteria, and the narrative uses the generic scoping line.
Objectives with no criteria: outcomes fall back to the objectives, verbatim.
Ready by plan and activity but no stated goals: outcomes are empty rather than invented.

objectives: Understand which funders require outcome reporting

note: The first objective begins with a capital: "set out to" must lower-case it so the sentence reads naturally.
Several objectives, none criteria: all become outcomes in order; only the first is named in the narrative, lower-cased.
